transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi... yeah, so, I came in because I just feel like I absolutely cannot get my schoolwork and my little accessories shop organized at the same time. It's just... everything is everywhere. My supplies, my due dates, receipts, assignment notes—they all just end up in these massive piles all over my room and my desk, and I honestly never know what to do first. 

Actually, speaking of the supplies, I just got this huge bulk order of glass beads for the shop. They're these really pretty iridescent star shapes? I was going to make phone charms out of them because that whole Y2K aesthetic is super popular right now. My friend Sarah told me I should be charging way more for them, but I feel bad overcharging people, you know? Especially since shipping is so expensive lately. But yeah, I completely lost the receipt for those star beads in one of my school notebooks... I think it was my history notebook, which is a whole other disaster because that professor just goes on and on and I can't even find where I wrote down the midterm date... but anyway, yeah, the piles are just getting out of control.
Do you find that you also struggle with staying organized or keeping track of things in parts of your life outside of school and your shop, like with personal relationships or daily routines?

Um... I don't really know? I haven't really thought about it. I mean, my morning routine is pretty standard, I guess. I get up, I make my coffee... well, actually, I just switched to matcha because regular iced coffee was making my stomach hurt so bad. I saw this girl on TikTok talking about how matcha has, like, L-theanine in it or something, and it's supposed to be way better for you? But honestly, it kind of tastes like literal grass unless you put a ton of vanilla syrup in it. 

I actually buy my syrup straight from this little local cafe down the street from my apartment. The barista there is super sweet, she always gives me a discount because I gave her one of my resin keychains once. They have this really cute outdoor patio area with all these fairy lights, it's such a good vibe when it gets warmer out... wait. What were you asking me? Something about my friends? I don't think I'm disorganized with my friends or my routine, really, if that's what you mean. I just haven't really noticed a problem with that stuff.
Have you ever found it hard to pay attention or stay focused on tasks or activities, even when they’re important or things you enjoy?

Oh, yeah, definitely. Like, when I'm in class or watching one of those video lectures for my business assignments? I can usually start out listening just fine, but then after a few minutes, my mind is completely somewhere else. I'll start thinking about new charm designs or, like, ideas for packing my orders. 

Actually, speaking of packing orders, I just found these amazing holographic bubble mailers online. They are so pretty, they literally look like a mermaid tail when the sun hits them! I bought a pack of fifty because I want my customers to have a really good unboxing experience, you know? Unboxing videos get so many views right now, and I even ordered custom pink tissue paper to match. But the tissue paper is taking literally forever to ship. The tracking hasn't updated in two weeks and it just says 'in transit' which is driving me crazy because I want to launch the new collection but I can't until the packaging is perfect... 

Wait, sorry. What was I talking about? Oh, right, the business videos. Yeah, so I'll be thinking about my shop designs or the mailers, and suddenly I realize the lecture video has been playing this whole time and I missed half of what was said. I always end up having to rewind it.
Do you also find it hard to stay focused during everyday activities, like chores, conversations, or while reading something for fun?

Um... I don't really think so? Like, I'm pretty okay with chores, I think. I mean, I try to do my laundry every Sunday. Well, except last Sunday because the washing machine in my building was completely broken. It was making this horrible screeching noise, like metal scraping against metal? 

My landlord is honestly the worst about fixing things. I had a leaky faucet for like three months before he finally sent a guy out, and the plumber he sent was this super grumpy older man who tracked mud all over my rug. Which was so annoying because I just bought that rug from Target. It's this really soft, fluffy cream color, and it ties my whole room together so perfectly. I've been trying to go for a more minimalist vibe in my apartment, even though my shop stuff kind of ruins the aesthetic. I saw this whole mood board on Pinterest for cream and sage green bedrooms and it looked so cozy... 

But yeah, wait, what did you ask? Chores and reading? I don't read a ton for fun anyway, mostly just scroll on my phone, so I haven't really noticed a problem with that kind of stuff.
Do you often feel restless, fidgety, or have trouble staying seated when you need to, like during classes or meetings?

Oh, yeah, definitely. It's actually kind of embarrassing sometimes? Like, when I have to sit through my business lectures or if I'm in a study group meeting, I literally cannot stay still. My leg will just start bouncing on its own, or I'll be clicking a pen over and over, or I'll just start messing with the beads and key rings I keep in my bag. I don't even realize I'm doing it until someone looks at me weird. 

Speaking of beads, I just got this huge shipment of these new glass star beads from this wholesale site. They are so pretty, they have this iridescent coating on them that catches the light perfectly. I'm planning to use them for a new line of phone charms. Phone charms are coming back in such a big way right now, everyone wants that Y2K aesthetic. I even bought a new phone case just so I could attach one of the prototypes I made. It's this really cute clear case with little strawberries painted on it, but the paint is already starting to chip off the corners, which is super annoying because it wasn't exactly cheap. I should probably leave a review about that, honestly. 

But anyway... what was I saying? Oh, right, the fidgeting. Yeah, I just can't seem to just sit there and do nothing with my hands or my legs when I'm supposed to be listening.
Do you ever find it hard to stay organized or keep track of things in your personal life, like remembering appointments, keeping up with plans, or managing your personal belongings?

Actually, yeah, that's kind of the main reason I came in to see you. I just feel like I absolutely cannot get my schoolwork and my little accessories shop organized at the same time. Like, my desk is a complete disaster. My shop supplies, due dates for my classes, receipts, assignment notes... they literally all just end up in these massive piles all over my room, and I stare at them and just don't know what to do first. 

Speaking of receipts, I actually just found one from Michaels from like two months ago at the bottom of one of the piles. I had bought all this UV resin because I wanted to try making custom initial keychains. Resin is so incredibly messy, by the way. I completely ruined my favorite pair of sweatpants last week doing it. They were those gray ones from Aerie with the crossover waistband? Everyone on TikTok was wearing them, so I finally caved and bought a pair, and they were so comfortable. But a huge glob of resin dripped right on the leg. I tried using rubbing alcohol to get it out because someone on Reddit said that works, but it honestly just smeared it and made it worse. Now I just wear them as pajamas, which is a bummer because they were kind of expensive for sweatpants. 

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, keeping track of things. Yeah, so between the business class notes and all my shop inventory, I just have piles everywhere and I can never figure out how to manage it all.
Have you ever had trouble keeping track of your personal belongings, like losing things frequently or forgetting where you put everyday items like your keys or phone?

Um, not really? I mean, I don't think I lose my stuff more than anyone else does. I always try to keep my keys on this specific hook by the door. Well, it's actually not a hook, it's this really cute little ceramic dish shaped like a mushroom that I got at a craft fair last summer. The girl selling them had an entire booth of just mushroom-themed pottery. She had these tiny little planters that looked like toadstools, and I almost bought one for my succulent, but my succulent actually died like three days before that. I think I overwatered it? I always do that. I read somewhere that you're only supposed to water them like once a month, but I just feel bad when the soil looks so dry, you know? It's like, how can a plant survive without water? 

My mom has this huge garden at her house and she grows all her own tomatoes and zucchini, and she's always trying to give me gardening advice, but I honestly just don't have the green thumb. She made this incredible zucchini bread last time I visited, though. It was so moist and she put chocolate chips in it, which sounds weird for a vegetable bread, but it totally works. I actually asked her for the recipe, but I haven't made it yet because I don't own a loaf pan. I looked on Amazon for one, but there are so many options and I didn't know if I should get silicone or metal... 

But yeah, wait, losing things? No, I usually know where my phone and keys are. I don't really have a big problem with that.
Can you think of times outside of school and your shop, like when you’re relaxing or spending time with friends, where you’ve struggled to stay focused or organized?

Well, I mean, if I'm just hanging out with friends, I guess it's not a huge issue because we're all just talking over each other anyway. But if I have to actually sit and focus on something, like... oh, like when I'm watching a video for my business class assignments. I can start out listening, totally fine, but then after like five minutes, my mind just completely wanders off. I'll start thinking about, you know, new charm designs or ideas for packaging orders. 

Actually, speaking of packaging, I just found these incredible holographic bubble mailers on this wholesale app. They are so pretty, they literally look like a rainbow when the sun hits them. I ordered a pack of 200 because it was a really good deal, but now I have this massive box sitting in my hallway and my roommate is kind of annoyed about it. She's super minimalist, like her entire side of the room is just beige and white, which I don't understand at all. How can you live without color? I feel like I need bright colors around me to feel energized. She bought this beige linen duvet cover that cost like two hundred dollars, and I'm just terrified I'm going to spill coffee on it or something because I'm always drinking iced lattes while I work. I actually bought an espresso machine off Facebook Marketplace last month so I could stop spending so much at Starbucks. It's one of those fancy ones with the milk frother? But the frother part is really tricky to clean, you have to soak it in hot water or the milk gets all crusty...

Wait, what was the question? Oh, right, struggling to focus. Yeah, so like in class or watching those business videos, I'll just zone out thinking about shop stuff, and then suddenly the video is over and I realize I completely missed half of what the professor even said.
Have you ever had periods of time where you felt down, sad, or hopeless, or lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

Um, no, not really. I don't think I've ever felt hopeless or anything like that. And I definitely don't lose interest in things I enjoy. Well, I mean, I guess I do bounce between different hobbies a lot, but it's not because I'm sad, I just get bored and want to try something new. 

Like, last month I was completely obsessed with making those chunky knit blankets. Have you seen those on Pinterest? You don't even use knitting needles, you literally just use your arms to weave this massive, fluffy yarn. I went to Joann Fabrics and bought like eight skeins of this beautiful sage green yarn. It was actually on sale, plus I had a coupon on their app. Their app is honestly so frustrating to use, though. It always freezes right when I get to the register, and the cashiers always look at me like I'm purposely holding up the line. But anyway, I started making the blanket on my living room floor, and it was going great, but then my roommate's cat, Barnaby—he's this huge orange tabby, literally the most chaotic animal I've ever met—he decided the yarn was his new best friend. He completely tangled it up while I was in the kitchen making a sandwich. I was making a turkey and provolone on sourdough. I just discovered this bakery down the street that makes the absolute best sourdough. It's perfectly crusty on the outside and they sell out by like noon every day, so you have to get there super early... 

Wait, sorry, what did you ask me? Oh, right, feeling sad. Yeah, no, I'm usually a pretty upbeat person! I don't really get depressed or anything, I just always have a lot going on.
Have you ever had times where you felt down or hopeless for several days in a row, or stopped caring about things you normally enjoy?

Um, I think you just asked me that? Or something really similar, right? But no, like I said, I don't really get down or hopeless for days at a time. I don't stop caring about things either. 

I mean, I care a lot about my shop and my friends. Oh, and my new espresso machine! I finally figured out how to clean the frother, by the way. I watched this YouTube tutorial by this guy who used to be a barista in Italy, and he said you have to purge the steam wand immediately after you use it, and then wipe it with a damp cloth. It sounds so obvious now, but I was just letting it sit there while I drank my coffee. The guy in the video had the most amazing kitchen, too. It had these gorgeous subway tiles and open shelving. I've always wanted open shelving, but my roommate hates the idea because she thinks it looks cluttered. Which, okay, fair, I do have a lot of mugs. I collect them from every place I travel to. My favorite one is from a trip to Seattle—it has the space needle on it and it changes color when you pour hot water in it. It's so cool. I went to Seattle right after high school with my best friend, and it rained the entire time, but we didn't even care because we just ate our way through Pike Place Market...

But yeah, no, I'm not really a sad or hopeless person. I don't have days where I just don't care about stuff.
Have you ever had a period lasting several days where you felt little pleasure in things you usually enjoy, or where even your favorite activities didn’t seem to cheer you up?

Okay, wait, didn't you just ask me that? Like, twice? I feel like we're going in circles here. But no, I really don't have days where I don't enjoy my favorite things. 

Like, I always love making jewelry for my shop. Always. Even when I'm tired. Actually, I was up until like 2 AM last night making these new resin earrings. They have actual dried flowers in them! I found this seller on Etsy who presses these tiny little forget-me-nots and daisies, and they're just the perfect size for the molds I use. The only problem with resin is that you have to be so careful about bubbles. I bought this heat gun to pop them, but it gets so hot, I accidentally melted the edge of one of my silicone molds. Which was super annoying because it was my favorite hexagon shape. I had to order a replacement, but the shipping is taking forever because it's coming from overseas. I track the package like three times a day, and it's been stuck in Chicago for a week. I don't know what's going on in Chicago, but their sorting center is where packages go to die. I've never actually been to Chicago, though. I hear the pizza is amazing, like the deep dish kind? I've always wanted to try it, but I'm kind of lactose intolerant, so I have to take those little pills before I eat cheese. I always forget them, though, and then I just suffer... 

But yeah, I don't lose pleasure in things. I definitely still love my hobbies and my shop!
Have you ever had a time when you felt down or sad for several days in a row, even when nothing bad was happening?

Okay, seriously, are you testing my memory or something? Because I swear you keep asking me the exact same thing! I feel like I'm in Groundhog Day. But no, I don't get sad for days in a row when nothing bad is happening. I really don't. 

Like I said, I'm just always moving onto the next thing. Speaking of moving, my friend Sarah is trying to move out of her apartment right now because her landlord is just the absolute worst. He refused to fix her dishwasher for like three months, and she's been washing everything by hand. Which, honestly, I hate washing dishes by hand. My skin gets so dry, especially in the winter. I have this amazing hand cream, though, it's made with shea butter and lavender. I found it at this little farmer's market last weekend. I love farmer's markets, but I always end up buying way too much stuff I don't need, like artisanal pickles. I bought this jar of spicy garlic pickles, and they are so good, but I ate like half the jar in one sitting and then I had the worst heartburn. I really need to stop doing that... 

But anyway, yeah, no days of just being sad for no reason! I'm good!

Can you describe a time when you had to complete a task that required sustained attention, like studying for an exam or preparing for a big project at your shop, and how well you were able to follow through from start to finish without getting distracted or losing focus?

Oh, following through from start to finish? Yeah, that’s... that's really hard. Like, if I’m in a class or when I'm watching a video for my business assignments—I'm trying to learn more about social media marketing right now—I can start out listening perfectly fine. But then, after just a few minutes, my mind is completely on new charm designs or ideas for my shop orders, and I suddenly realize I missed half of what was said. 

Speaking of charm designs, I actually just found this amazing wholesale supplier that sells these tiny little enameled frogs. They are so cute, they have little lily pads and everything! I think frogs are making a huge comeback, you know? Like that whole cottagecore aesthetic. My roommate actually tried to paint a giant frog on her bedroom wall last week. Well, it was supposed to be a frog, but the green paint she used was way too neon, so it kind of looks like a radioactive alien. We tried to cover it up with a giant tapestry, but you can still see its weird little feet sticking out at the bottom. We get a lot of our tapestries and posters from this vintage shop downtown. The guy who runs it is so nice, he always gives us a discount because I gave him a pair of my custom earrings once for his daughter's birthday. She turned twelve, I think? Or maybe thirteen. Thirteen is such a weird age, I remember when I was thirteen I went through this phase where I only wore clothing that was black and white stripes... 

Wait, what was the question again? Something about studying?
Have you ever lost interest in activities or hobbies that you used to really enjoy, even if you still do them?

Okay, are you messing with me? Because I'm pretty sure you've asked me about not liking my hobbies like three times now! I feel like I'm taking a pop quiz where every question is the same, but worded slightly differently to trick me. But no, I haven't lost interest in my hobbies. I still love them! 

Like, I was just talking about my resin jewelry, right? I actually have this whole new idea for a collection based on, like, vintage circus themes. I found these tiny little brass charms shaped like carousel horses and Ferris wheels, and I want to embed them in clear resin with a little bit of gold flake. Gold flake is so messy, though! The last time I used it, I sneezed and it literally went everywhere. My cat, Barnaby, walked through it, and he was sparkling for like a week. He looked so glamorous, honestly. He's an orange tabby, and he's super chunky, so he just looked like this giant, sparkly cheese puff walking around the apartment. We tried to give him a bath to get it off, but he absolutely hates water. He turned into a demon and scratched my roommate's arm. We had to buy her these special bandages that have Neosporin already on the pad. I didn't even know they made those! They're so convenient. I usually just buy the cheap store-brand bandaids, but they never stick right, especially if you're washing your hands a lot. And I wash my hands constantly when I'm working with resin because it gets so sticky...

But yeah, no, I definitely haven't lost interest in my stuff! I'm still obsessed with it.
Have you ever had a time when you felt down or hopeless, even when everything in your life seemed to be going okay?

Okay, seriously, are you writing this down? Because I feel like I'm taking crazy pills here! You literally just asked me about being sad for no reason, like, five minutes ago! I promise you, my answer hasn't changed. No, I don't get down or hopeless when everything is fine. I'm totally fine! 

I'm actually feeling really good today because the weather is finally getting warmer. I hate the cold so much. It makes my joints ache, which is weird because I'm only twenty-one, right? My grandma used to complain about her joints all the time, especially her knees. She had this crazy collection of vintage teacups that she kept in this huge glass cabinet. When I was little, I was terrified I was going to bump into it and break everything. She had this one cup that had tiny little hand-painted roses on it, and it was so delicate it felt like it was made of paper. I love roses, but they're so hard to keep alive. I bought a mini rose bush for my windowsill last month, and it died in like three days. I think I overwatered it. Or maybe underwatered it? I can never remember which one causes the leaves to turn yellow. I watched a whole YouTube video about plant care, but halfway through the guy started talking about his trip to Costa Rica, and then I ended up watching videos of sloths for like two hours. Sloths are so weird, right? They move so slowly... 

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, being sad. Yeah, no, definitely not sad!
Can you recall a time in the past few months—outside of school or your shop—where you had trouble staying focused or organized, even during something you were looking forward to or found important?

Trouble staying focused outside of school or the shop? Um, I don't really think so? Like, I can't really think of a specific time... I mean, I guess if I'm doing something I actually want to do, I'm usually pretty into it. 

Like, my friend Sarah had this huge birthday dinner last weekend at this new Italian place downtown. It was supposed to be super important because she was introducing her new boyfriend to everyone. He's a graphic designer, which is so cool because I've been wanting to learn Illustrator to make better logos for my shop. Right now I just use Canva, and it's okay, but you can definitely tell it's, like, a template, you know? Anyway, we were at the restaurant, and they brought out this massive bowl of truffle fries. Have you ever had truffle oil? It smells so strong, almost like gasoline, but in a good way? My roommate hates it. She says it smells like old socks. She has this weird thing about smells, she can't even walk down the detergent aisle at the grocery store without getting a headache. We usually have to buy the unscented laundry pods, which are so boring. I like the ones that smell like lavender or ocean breeze. I went to the beach once when I was little, and I found this huge conch shell, but when I picked it up, a crab crawled out and pinched my finger! I screamed so loud my dad dropped his ice cream cone in the sand... 

Wait. Were you asking about a specific event? I don't think I've had trouble focusing on important stuff, no.
In the past few weeks, have you had days where you felt little pleasure or joy, even when doing things you usually enjoy, like working on your shop or hanging out with friends?

Okay, seriously, are you doing this on purpose? Because I feel like I'm stuck in a time loop! I swear you've asked me about not enjoying things, like, four times now! I'm totally fine! I still love doing my stuff and hanging out with my friends. No days where I just don't feel joy or whatever. 

Like, I was just hanging out with Sarah yesterday, and we went to this thrift store that just opened up near campus. It's huge, like, it used to be an old roller rink, I think? You can still see the wooden floorboards where they used to skate. I always wanted to learn how to roller skate, but I have terrible balance. I tried ice skating once in middle school, and I literally fell on my butt within five seconds. It was so embarrassing because this guy I had a crush on, Tyler, was there, and he just laughed at me. He had this really cool jacket with patches all over it, and I actually bought a bunch of iron-on patches recently to put on my denim jacket. I got one that looks like a UFO beaming up a cow, and another one that's a slice of pizza. Pizza sounds so good right now. There's this place down the street that does a dollar slice night on Tuesdays, and the crust is perfectly crispy. But you have to get there early or the line goes around the block, and waiting in line is the absolute worst. I get so fidgety if I have to stand still for too long...

But yeah, no, I'm definitely not having any issues enjoying things! I feel fine.
